steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I feel weird saying this, but if the heating's still chugging along and the stove's lit too, why does it feel so cold? The bank's not up to something again, are they?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I hung them up all night and my socks still ain't dry.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Hm? What's that noise?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: How many times do I have to tell you to shave, Woody? Every time you take a sip of water, you spill droplets all over the table.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What are you on about? I ain't had a drink since I came in.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Then where did all these water stains come from?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Your diner's just getting old and rickety. Just like my brain these days...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Like, am I remembering this wrong, or has there always been a huge water stain over there?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: The pipes— The water pipes ruptured?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Oh my god... No way my run-down old floorboards can handle all this water damage!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Go and turn off the valve, then look for something to catch the water leaking in. I'll take care of things upstairs!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: My poor waist... I can barely even stand up straight. How're things looking up there, Woody?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I suggest you grab a chair and sit down before I tell you. You ain't as spry as you used to be.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Spare me the theatrics and just lay it on me. I've seen it all by now.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's flooded up to my knees, and all the furniture's ruined.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...What about my clothes in the wardrobe? Are they okay?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Your favorite color is red, right?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I hope this is good news...?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Mm, perfect. The water from the pipe's all rust-colored, so I'm guessing all your clothes will be, too.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...So, what the hell were you doing up there all this time?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Grabbing all this.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Oh... I almost forgot about this box. Where'd you find it?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Where else? In the wardrobe. Not like you have anywhere else to hide stuff. I also grabbed a few things off your nightstand.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: *sigh*... At least there's no water inside. Now let's take a look...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Here's the insurance policy. Should cover today's damages. Also the deed to the land, the house, and... my passbook.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Why're you still hanging onto that? You know you'll never touch none of that money.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Would you throw it away, if you were me?

spans.text: throw it away, if you were me?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: See, you get what I'm talking about, don't you? What he saved up all these years wasn't just the money. It was his conviction too.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Tch. Sentimental old fool.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: We're all old fools here, Woody. Compared to the fickle future, the pieces of the past we've built up over the years hit that much closer to home.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Says you.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Look, it's the novel that was sitting on the nightstand, too. Ain't been opened for the longest time.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: The same old clichéd love story about a rich girl and some farmer.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Why you gotta be so grumpy? Ain't got nothing nice to say?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I've got plenty. Like, good luck at the bank tomorrow.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...You should thank your lucky stars I've mellowed with age. So, what about you? Any plans for tomorrow?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I'm gonna bring Jessica along to have a talk with someone.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: A talk?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Yup, just your normal talk.

steps.name: Boorish Brute
steps.text: P-Put the gun down, yeah? If you've got something to say, old man, I'm listening.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What're you so scared of? If you ask me, I'm as gentle as they come.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So, you wanna chat? Let's chat. You and the bandits out there have been meeting up in secret these last few days. How about you share what you talked about?

steps.name: Boorish Brute
steps.text: Let go of me, old man! I said... I said...

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: You spineless wimp!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Give him a good kick, Jessica.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Umm, okay...

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: What are you doing? Wiping your shoes on my pants?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...Forget it, Jessica. How's your aim?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: N-Not too bad, I think.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Perfect. Can you thread a bullet right between his ears?

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: Aaaaaargh!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: S-Sorry, sir, my hand is... still a bit shaky. But it's not like I hit you with that last one, so you can stop screaming.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's fine. You'll get it after a few tries.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: A-Alright!

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: It... It was...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It was what?

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: It was because they've been short on manpower these days, so they're trying to recruit us. I figured, seeing how none of us on the plate can repay our debts anyway, might as well give some folks a chance to dig themselves out.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You're talking about converting people to a life of banditry?

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: It's.. It's not like I forced them or anything. They were ready to jump ship before I even finished talking.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: C'mon, like I said, what are you fellas so afraid of? Just tell me the truth.

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: ...Says the man waving a gun in my face. What if we say something that pisses you off?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Where are those bandits hiding now?

steps.name: Rude Ruffian
steps.text: H-How would I know? They're so damn slippery...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: That's enough, Jessica.

steps.name: Boorish Brute
steps.text: Just let us go already, old man. You can take anything you want from this room, please...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Color me surprised. These punks actually have some pretty nice stuff. Even got some bottles of beer and champagne in the corner.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Did we seriously just... let them walk away scot-free?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: All I care about is finding those missing people. If these punks wanna leave the plate, that's their call. I'm ain't gonna judge them for it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But, I think...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Want something to drink?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I think I'll pass.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...Hm. Mellow, full-bodied fragrance of hops, and a refreshing aftertaste... Where the hell did they get such quality booze?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: My sincerest apologies, Helena, ma'am. After a preliminary review and discussion, we cannot accept your compensation application. The damage to the water pipes in your incident photos is clearly manmade.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Manmade? Wait... You mean, someone's messing with us again?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Considering your restaurant's revenue and liabilities, we have ample reason to believe that you deliberately damaged your own water system to cash out on the insurance plan.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...You think this is insurance fraud?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: No, ma'am, we're simply saying it's a reasonable conclusion to make. As long as you can provide professional proof that eliminates that possibility, we'll be able to move on to the claims process.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: How the hell am I supposed to find a judge or a lawyer on this damn plate?! It's been ages since they all left!

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: My apologies, but we're simply following procedure. If that's all, then I'd like to assist the next customer. There's a long line behind you.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Then... Withdraw the money from this passbook.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: This passbook... Yes, this jogs my memory. You've already applied several times before, but can you prove that you came by this source of income legally?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: He sent me this passbook along with a letter, but by the time I arrived in Davistown, he'd already passed away! All his neighbors can attest to that!

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Do you really expect that to hold up, legally speaking?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Just gimme back my stuff. I'm leaving.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: All your belongings are right here. Remember to take them with you, ma'am. Also, may I offer you a little reminder?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Based on the photos you provided, we can only guarantee one thing: the flooding to your restaurant has significantly reduced its value. Meaning it is no longer enough to offset your existing debts.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: If you don't want to enter the compulsory liquidation process, I recommend you consider the following—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I've heard enough... Just keep your trap shut, bastard.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Helena?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Looks like she didn't notice us.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Why are there so many people here today? What's the bank up to?

steps.name: Anxious Elderly Woman
steps.text: This is the collection notice I received earlier this morning. It says that I'm insolvent and will be declared bankrupt soon, but I've been making my payments...

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Ma'am, we've been extending your loan term so far, but we're no longer able to grant you leniency.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: The good news is that after liquidating your existing assets, your remaining balance will be only two thousand gold certificates. Which I'm sure you'll have no trouble procuring?

steps.name: Anxious Elderly Woman
steps.text: Please, can you extend it just another two months? No, one month is enough.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Unfortunately, no. We can't push it back even a single day.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: If you're unable to make your payment, we'll have no choice but to begin the compulsory process.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: All your property will be confiscated, and you'll have to leave Davistown within the time allotted. While continuing to pay your debt of roughly ten thousand certs, of course. Failure to do so will result in criminal liability.

steps.name: Anxious Elderly Woman
steps.text: But I can't afford that! Whether it's two or ten thousand! Please, I beg you, just one more month's grace!

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: If you truly have no other options, then please take a look at this.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: ...The Pioneer Plan. If you apply now, you'll be able to enjoy a certain amount of loan forgiveness.

steps.name: Anxious Elderly Woman
steps.text: But I'm already so old. Even if I went out the frontier, what could I possibly do?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Are you in any position to worry about that?

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Will you continue to carry your debt at the risk of criminal liability and lose the roof over your head, or would you rather shed some of your debt and start a new life on the frontier? ...Do you really need to hear my opinion?

steps.name: Anxious Elderly Woman
steps.text: I'll sign it.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Excellent. Please head to your right. My colleagues there will help you get signed up.

steps.name: Bank Employee
steps.text: Next customer!

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: What... What the hell is this...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: If you two are here to discuss business, please get in line—

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Oh, if it isn't Miss Liskarm and Miss Franka. How are you doing? Have you finished looking over the list?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You've got some explaining to do! Why are you forcing people out into the barrens?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: By signing the agreement, they can shed a lot of their existing debt and start over without that weight on their backs. Isn't that the best possible outcome?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: ...And what about the list? How are any of these people supposed to be bandits? They're just a bunch of destitute old folks who don't want to be run out of their homes!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Once they go bankrupt, their houses no longer belong to them, but rather to us, the creditors. What else would you call it when someone takes advantage of the lack of police to squat on someone else's property? Is that not a crime?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So your so-called 'law and order' is just driving out poor people who can't pay up?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: There's nothing 'so-called' about it. That is law and order, Miss Franka.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Insurance fraud?! ...They're declaring you bankrupt?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That's why I didn't wanna talk about it. I feel like I'm gonna pop a blood vessel.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If the bank is purposely depreciating the value of the diner, how much are they slashing it by?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I've been going back and forth with them for a while now, but seems like they're settling at fifty thousand certs.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If it's only fifty thousand, I can... lend you the rest.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Just like you secretly 'lent' money to Leone?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sylvia told you?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: It's been eating her up inside, so she told me this morning. Don't worry though, I can keep a secret.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: If you want to lend me money, of course I'd accept it. But who knows how long it'll take to pay it back, if ever.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't mind, even if you never pay it back.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No, stop it... Don't say things like that. I'll definitely find a way to return the favor someday.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Here. When the bank comes to collect, give them this check. Sorry...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: *sigh*... And why are you apologizing? It ain't like you're the one borrowing money.

spans.text: apologizing? It ain't like you're the one borrowing money.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: By the way, one other thing. Leone was too embarrassed to tell you himself, but he wanted me to pass this on.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: He found out about the money?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You silly girl... I told you, your secret's safe with me. Why would I tell him? He just wants to treat you to a meal.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Seems like bandits ain't the only thing Woodrow's been tracking. He's got a good catch of fowlbeasts. Miles and Benny'll be there too.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Oh, okay then...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You don't sound too happy about it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's because... Actually, I saw a lot of people outside the bank on my way here. They were signing agreements... to head out to the frontier.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I asked around, and it seems like it's a way of shedding some of their debt.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But why do they have to abandon everything and risk their lives to start over in a place with nothing, just for a little bit of debt relief?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Can they... even survive that ordeal?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: And last but not least, the main course. Garlic-crusted fowlbeast with roast potatoes.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Whoa, that smells amazing...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I'll have this piece.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Put it down, Woody. That's for Jessica.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You heard her. She's the star of tonight's feast.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's no big deal. I just saw what was going on in Davistown and felt that I couldn't sit back and watch... As for the food, I'm fine with whatever, really. I even had some biscuits earlier, so I'm not that hungry.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: See, she's fine with it.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No means no. Benny, this one's for you.

steps.name: Benny
steps.text: Oh, wow... Th-Thank you very much.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Tch...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What's so funny?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: N-Nothing. It just occurred to me how different you seem, compared to when we first met.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Yeah... He's been like that for ages. When he first strolled in town, he immediately pissed off pretty much everyone in the mines. We all thought that this grumpy, sharp-tongued asshole was here to cause trouble.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And what happened after that?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Then, he met Helena.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: He really should be thanking her. If it weren't for her warmth and willingness to put in a few good words for him with those unlikable fellas...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: But chat a bit today, and you'll find common ground tomorrow. In the end, she discovered his more... charming side, and showed it off to the others.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: There was even a song going around at that time, probably written by one of her admirers. Still remember how it goes, Miles?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Oh yeah, I almost forgot... Right, there was that song. I think it's coming back to me.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Give us the intro, and let's sing it together—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Who gave you jerks permission to sing in my restaurant—

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪I wandered here alone, not a penny to my name♪

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪My hometown far behind me, miles and miles away♪

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪The barrens stretch before me, as far as I can see♪

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ♪And who's waiting at the end, who indeed but she♪

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ♪She spread her arms, spread her heart, showed me that pretty face♪

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ♪And from that moment on, I found my dreams in her embrace♪

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Is this song... about Helena?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Who else?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If you ask me... the 'her' it mentions might not be a specific person, but rather a broader idea.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: What sort of idea?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Maybe this 'she' is a home filled with everyone's dreams. Davistown itself.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Hey, that makes sense!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Think about it. The second verse talks about her 'body,' right? That's the energy tower. Her 'hair' is the white smoke coming from it, and her 'burning heart' must be the plant's furnace.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: And, in that section you fellas just sang, with her 'arms' and her 'embrace'? Ain't that just like those two long railroad tracks... embracing everyone here?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So many pioneers carved out this piece of land, bit by bit, with the tools in their hands. It'd become the place they started their families and businesses in.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: And after that, even more youngsters arrived with their dreams and aspirations, following the footsteps of the previous generation and pitching in their youth and passion.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: 'She,' and only 'she,' is worthy of everyone's admiration.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I knew it... I knew it!

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: It all makes sense now!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Anyhow, no way in hell anybody's pinning all their hopes and dreams on my body.
The engineer has nothing more to say. His eyelids droop and his head tilts back slightly, the restaurant owner's words whisking him back to the past.

a.text: He remembers the soot-stained faces of his coworkers when they went home after a long shift. He remembers how his neighbors would greet him in the morning when he left for work.
He remembers the cool and refreshing beer foam escaping from the rim of his glass, and the warmth on his cheeks from the children's kisses.
His thoughts are wild and turbulent, but they fill his heart with warmth and comfort.
Just like the song he is humming right now. Completely tuneless, yet moving nevertheless.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪And who's waiting at the end, who indeed but she♪

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪She spread her arms, spread her heart, showed me that pretty face♪

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ♪And from that moment on, I found my dreams in her embrace♪
The others in the room stop what they are doing, and make no other sounds. Only the engineer's voice is allowed to fill the entire restaurant.
After a while, the boiler worker's coarse voice joins the song, and the restaurant owner begins to hum along softly.
Even Woodrow, whose attention had been seized by the food on his plate, cannot help but tap his fingertips against his knees to the beat.
Only Jessica feels gripped by an inexplicable unease, as if there is a dark shadow in her heart that will not go away.
